tex_content.html:
Therefore \[ \pi (\xi ,\tau )=\frac{R\xi }{R+\tau },\qquad |\pi (\xi ,\tau )|^2=R^2\frac{\tau ^2-R^2}{(\tau +R)^2}<R^2, \] \[ \pi ^{-1}(u)=\left(\frac{2R^2u}{R^2-|u|^2},\frac{R(R^2+|u|^2)}{R^2-|u|^2}\right), \] and \[ (\pi ^{-1})^*\bar g_R=\frac{4R^4\sum _j(du^j)^2}{(R^2-|u|^2)^2}. \]

The generalized Cayley map $\kappa :\mathbb U^n(R)\to \mathbb B^n(R)$ is, in dimension two, \begin{equation} \kappa (z)=iR\frac{z-iR}{z+iR},\tag {3.14} \end{equation} and in real coordinates, with $x\in \mathbb R^{n-1}$, \begin{equation} \kappa (x,y)=\left(\frac{2R^2x}{|x|^2+(y+R)^2},R\frac{|x|^2+|y|^2-R^2}{|x|^2+(y+R)^2}\right).\tag {3.15} \end{equation} Its inverse is \[ \kappa ^{-1}(u,v)=\left(\frac{2R^2u}{|u|^2+(v-R)^2},R\frac{R^2-|u|^2-v^2}{|u|^2+(v-R)^2}\right), \] and direct substitution gives $\kappa ^*\bar g_R^{\mathbb B}=\bar g_R^{\mathbb U}$. □

We use $\mathbb H^n(R)$ for any model in the theorem and $\bar g_R$ for its corresponding metric; $R=1$ is denoted $(\mathbb H^n,\bar g)$.
